title: Why Shares of Lindblad Expeditions Are Rocketing Higher Today
author: Scott Levine
description: Lindblad Expeditions stock surged 11.4% after reporting strong Q2 2026 results with $199.2 million in revenue (beating $185.9 million expectations) and a net loss of $0.02 per share (better than anticipated $0.11 loss). The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $830-850 million from $800-830 million, achieved record net yield of $1,294 and 91% occupancy. However, the analyst cautions that at 247x forward earnings and a 52-week high valuation, investors should wait for a pullback.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company beat revenue expectations ($199.2M vs $185.9M expected), surpassed earnings expectations (loss of $0.02 vs $0.11 expected), achieved record Q2 net yield and occupancy rates, raised full-year revenue guidance, and showed 31% year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth. However, the analyst notes extreme valuation at 247x forward earnings warrants caution.

title: A Lindblad Expeditions Director Sold Nearly 53,000 Shares Worth $1.2 Million. Here's a Deeper Look at the Transaction.
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: Lindblad Expeditions director L. Dyson Dryden sold 52,747 shares worth approximately $1.2 million on May 29, 2026, representing 5.07% of his direct holdings. The sale occurred after the stock had risen 118.8% year-over-year, suggesting profit-taking following substantial share price appreciation. Despite the sale, Dryden retained over 988,000 shares, indicating continued confidence in the company.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the insider sale could signal profit-taking concerns, the company demonstrates strong fundamentals with Q1 revenue up 16% YoY, net income jumping to $6 million, and positive 2026 revenue guidance ($800-850 million). The director's retention of 988,000 shares suggests continued confidence. The stock's 118.8% year-over-year gain and subsequent 52-week high of $26.56 indicate positive market sentiment, but insider selling warrants a neutral stance rather than purely positive.

title: This $4 Million Rental Stock Buy Signals Confidence in Data Center Demand
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: Anchor Capital Management increased its stake in McGrath RentCorp by 40,352 shares ($4.49 million) in Q1 2026, signaling confidence in data center demand. McGrath's rental operations revenue climbed 5%, with TRS-RenTelco rental revenue jumping 13% due to accelerating data center buildouts. The company maintains a 35-year dividend increase streak and offers exposure to infrastructure spending with recurring revenue.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Anchor Capital's increased investment signals confidence in the company's growth prospects, particularly in data center demand. Strong Q1 results show 5% rental revenue growth and 13% growth in TRS-RenTelco segment. The company's 35-year dividend increase streak and stable adjusted EBITDA demonstrate financial strength and shareholder-friendly policies, despite broader market underperformance.

title: What to Know About This Fund’s $14 Million Patrick Industries Exit After a Tough Quarter
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: Anchor Capital Management fully exited its position in Patrick Industries during Q1 2026, selling 116,967 shares worth approximately $14.46 million. The exit reduced Patrick Industries from 11.3% of the fund's assets to zero. Patrick Industries faces headwinds from softening RV and housing demand, though the company showed strength in marine and powersports segments with revenue of $997 million and maintained solid free cash flow of $194 million.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The fund's complete exit of an 11.3% position signals loss of confidence. Stock has plunged nearly 40% since February and underperformed S&P 500 by 17 percentage points. While the company maintains operational strength and free cash flow, macro pressures in RV and housing markets are weighing on investor sentiment.
